newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cotton weekly export sales highlights--USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cotton weekly export sales highlights--USDA.

text.p: USDA cotton export sales highlights in latest reporting week:

Net Upland sales were the lowest of the marketing year with reductions of 20,000 running bales (RB). Increases for Indonesia (4,500 RB), Taiwan (4,400 RB), Mexico (3,400 RB), and Brazil (2,700 RB) were more than offset by reductions for Russia (35,300 RB) and Japan (5,900 RB).
Sales of 23,200 RB for delivery during the 1997/98 marketing year were primarily for Indonesia (6,900 RB), Peru (4,400 RB), Brazil (4,400 RB), and Mexico (4,000 RB).
Exports of 128,500 RB exceeded the previous week by 4 percent, but were 2 percent below of the 4-week average.

Asian destinations accounted for 53 percent of the week's shipments; Western Hemisphere, 29 percent; and West European, 18 percent. The major recipients were Turkey (20,200 RB), China (19,500 RB), Mexico (15,700 RB), and South Korea (13,400 RB).
